balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Republic Services, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Republic Services, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Republic Services, Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Republic Services, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Republic Services, Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Republic Services, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Republic Services, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Republic Services, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenueMix.title: Revenue by line of business
revenueMix.content:
Total revenue split into the lines Republic reports each quarter: Collection (residential, small-container, large-container), Landfill (net disposal/tipping fees), Environmental Solutions (industrial/hazardous waste, PFAS-impacted material, field services), Transfer and Recycling commodity sales.

For Republic Services, Inc.: Collection is ~68% of revenue and grows with core pricing and municipal contract wins; Environmental Solutions (built out since the 2022 US Ecology acquisition) is the fastest-growing line, management says its PFAS-related revenue is already running ahead of the ~$100m FY2026 target, and is targeted at 15-20% annual growth. Recycling commodity revenue is the smallest and most volatile line, swinging with OCC/plastics/metals prices rather than volume.

What to watch:

  • Environmental Solutions growing faster than Collection, shifting the mix toward a higher-growth, less-penetrated niche
  • Recycling commodity swings that are price, not volume, driven
  • Landfill revenue tracking tipping-fee pricing more than tonnage

segmentEbitda.title: Segment adjusted EBITDA
segmentEbitda.content:
Republic reports Recycling & Waste in two geographic groups plus Environmental Solutions as a third segment: Group 1 covers the western US, Group 2 the southeastern/midwestern US, eastern seaboard and Canada, and Environmental Solutions is managed nationally.

For Republic Services, Inc.: Group 1 and Group 2 are similarly sized and carry the bulk of segment EBITDA from the mature collection/landfill network; Environmental Solutions is smaller but its margin trajectory is the one management points to most often when discussing mix-driven margin expansion, alongside headline adjusted EBITDA margin which compressed to 31.8% in Q3 2026 from 32.8% a year earlier on fuel and healthcare cost inflation.

What to watch:

  • Environmental Solutions EBITDA growing faster than its revenue (operating leverage as PFAS volumes scale)
  • Either geographic group lagging on route density or weather/labor disruption

pricingVolume.title: Core price, yield, volume and internal growth
pricingVolume.content:
Core price is the price increase Republic pushes through on total revenue, net of rollbacks and discounts; average yield is an alternative realized-price measure; volume growth is the revenue impact of tonnage/customer-count change; internal growth is core price plus volume -- organic growth before M&A.

For Republic Services, Inc.: core price has been normalizing down from the elevated 5.9% full-year 2025 rate to 5.3% in both Q2 and Q3 2026, while volume has been improving from roughly -1.6% in Q2 2026 to only -0.6% in Q3 2026 -- pricing is still running well ahead of volume declines, which is the oligopoly's central economic logic.

What to watch:

  • Core price decelerating faster than volume recovers (internal growth compressing)
  • Core price vs. average yield diverging (mix or discounting effects)
  • Volume turning positive as construction/industrial activity recovers

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Republic Services, Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Republic Services, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
